title: ONE YEAR. ONE SECOND.
logline: An unofficial, photoreal Jägermeister spec film told only through objects, places and light. Sixty-three years of patience pass in time-lapse: a typewritten secret in Wolfenbüttel in 1934, a year in oak, an ocean crossed, and America's ice-cold ritual. Then, in a lakeside bar at Lake Tahoe around 1997, one second stretches into seven as a shot glass plunges into an unbranded energy drink and the Jägerbomb is born (or so the story goes). A year in oak. A second in glass.
visual_language:
INTENT: This should look like a high-end spirits commercial shot on a cinema camera, not a CG showreel. References: whisky and cognac films, Dutch still-life painting (Kalf, Claesz), deep chiaroscuro darkness, and 1000 fps beverage cinematography. It is the opposite of the rejected film: no forest, no particles, no gold, no glow, no line art, no flying camera and no black studio void. Every frame sits in a real place, and every light comes from a source you could rig on a set.

THE TIME DEVICE. The film has two time signatures:
- Time-lapse compresses 63 years of history (three days of maceration, a year in a cellar).
- Extreme slow motion stretches the single legendary second to about seven.
The tagline closes the idea: "A year in oak. A second in glass."

EDITORIAL SPINE: three circle match cuts carry the eras.
1. The red GEHEIM rubber stamp becomes the head of an oak cask.
2. The cellar's round oculus window becomes a ship's porthole.
3. The pendant-lamp reflection in a freshly poured shot becomes the full moon over Lake Tahoe.
Every cut lands on the 96 BPM beat grid (15 frames per beat). Every era change lands on a bar downbeat.

FORMAT AND LENS
- 2.39:1 scope. Render 1920x804 and letterbox inside a 1920x1080 master. The 138 px bars carry subtitles and legal text, never the picture.
- Blender camera: 36 mm sensor, horizontal fit. Lenses: 35, 50, 65, 85 and 100 mm macro, at f/1.8 to f/5.6. All scenes are built at true metric scale (a shot glass is 6 cm tall), so real f-stops give real macro depth of field.
- Anamorphic bokeh: circular aperture (0 blades) with Cycles aperture ratio 1.5. A ratio above 1 gives the vertical oval of real anamorphic glass; this corrects the 0.66 used in one concept.
- Racks: keyframed focus empties, with about 1.5% focal-length change during each rack to simulate lens breathing.
- Camera motion is motion-control only: Bezier-eased slides of 2-40 cm, slow push-ins, locked-off frames and one dolly-and-boom. There are no orbits, no drone moves and no fly-throughs. A noise modifier adds 0.05° of breathing so no frame is CG-still.

COMPOSITING LENS FINISH
- 0.5% barrel distortion with 0.3% dispersion.
- Red-tinted halation on hot highlights (Glare fog glow, low mix).
- 15% vignette.
- Animated, luma-weighted procedural 35mm grain over everything (it also hides denoiser residue).
- 0.2 px gate weave.
- AgX view transform, graded in comp.

LIGHT AND PALETTE BY ERA (motivated practicals only)
- 1934 workroom: low winter dawn through an east mullioned window, an enamel desk lamp. Scrubbed oak #3B2A1E, card stock #E3D9C3, sage herbs, saffron red, tarnished brass. Shadows lifted slightly toward green-black.
- Cellar: whitewashed brick and umber oak. The sun disc through the oculus changes colour with the seasons: winter 7500K, summer 5200K, autumn 3800K.
- 1970s hold: a 2700K caged bulb, chipped green paint over rust, a steel-blue sea in the porthole.
- 1980s back bar: 4000K fluorescent on brushed steel and frost, with a red neon smear.
- Tahoe c.1997, at summer blue hour (no snow anywhere): indigo window, moon-white glade, bare granite ridges with the last alpenglow, knotty-pine amber, a pink neon "OPEN" (#FF4F9A) and 2700K enamel pendants.
- Hero colours are kept for the two liquids only: Jägermeister is mahogany-black with ruby edges; the energy drink is pale gold-green.
- No orange rim lights. Backlight is always the cool moon window.

REALISM RULES
- Bevel every edge 0.5-3 mm.
- Measured refractive indices: glass 1.52, energy drink 1.34, Jägermeister 1.355.
- Imperfection masks everywhere: dust on up-facing surfaces, smudged glass roughness, chipped paint, varnish scratches, chalk breakup.
- Every repeated object gets its own random seed. Piles are settled with rigid bodies, never placed by hand.
- Nothing floats in the air unless physics put it there.
- People are always implied, never shown: typebars striking (keys out of frame), a fresh chalk mark, a stool still turning, a ring of frost where a glass stood, the shadow of a lifted shot glass.

TYPOGRAPHY: documentary and restrained. Only fonts installed on the render machine (checked with fc-list): Courier 10 Pitch (a real typewriter face), Inter Display, Inter, JetBrains Mono and Liberation Sans.
- Bone white #ECE6DA, plus one thin rule in Jäger orange #E8601C on the end card.
- No serif display face, no Fraktur, no Cinzel, no gold, no glow, no light sweep, no callout graphics.
- Most text lives inside the world: the typed recipe card, the stamp, chalk, crate stencils, neon and the bottle label.

sets.name: A — Mast's Workroom, Wolfenbüttel 1934 (S01-S05)
sets.build:
SHELL: build only what the lenses see, a 4x3 m corner.
- Two lime-plaster walls: Principled shader, two-scale noise for colour and bump, damp mottling at the base.
- Plank floor in deep shadow.
- East window, 3x4 panes: bevelled oak mullions and transom, putty lines, one cracked pane. Crown glass uses a low-frequency noise normal for waviness and IOR 1.52.
- Frame the mullion shadows as diagonal bars. Never compose them as a centred cross.

WORKBENCH: 2.0 x 0.8 x 0.07 m with 2 mm bevels.
- Scrubbed-oak shader: wave plus noise growth rings, stretched-Voronoi medullary flecks, knife-score lines, grime in cavities from a pointiness/AO mask.
- Baked once to 4K albedo, roughness and normal maps.
- Brown kraft paper sheets on the bench: fibre noise and crease displacement.

TYPEWRITER MACRO RIG (S01). Only the 30° of the mechanism the lens sees:
- 9 typebars: 1.2 mm bevelled steel levers on pivot pins.
- Slugs with raised, mirrored glyphs extruded 0.3 mm from Courier 10 Pitch outlines.
- Slotted segment arc and a bent-sheet ribbon vibrator.
- 8 mm two-tone black/red cloth ribbon: crossed wave-texture weave bump, sheen 0.3.
- Ø32 mm rubber platen (roughness 0.55, wear noise) and paper-bail rollers.
- 200 gsm card: subdivided plane, fibre bump, 10% translucency.
- Card artwork drawn with PIL at 4096 px in Courier 10 Pitch, with per-glyph ink density, ribbon-weave texture inside the glyphs and baseline wobble.
  - Header: 'KRÄUTERLIKÖR — REZEPTUR — C. MAST — WOLFENBÜTTEL 1934'.
  - Below: a numbered list, every ingredient overtyped XXXXXXXX.
  - Round red GEHEIM rubber stamp in Liberation Sans Bold, ink breakup and edge pooling.
- Glyph impressions drive a bump map so the strikes catch the light.

BOTANICAL KIT: Geometry Nodes generators, each seeded per instance.
- Star anise: 8 radial boat-shaped carpels with glossy seeds.
- Cinnamon: curled bark sheet along a spiral, with solidify and layered broken edges.
- Cardamom: ellipsoid with wave-texture ridges and pale-green translucency.
- Juniper: blue-black spheres with a waxy bloom from sheen plus coat roughness 0.4.
- Saffron: curves with flared trumpet tips in deep-red subsurface.
- Chamomile: Voronoi-bumped dome with arrayed petals.
- Bitter-orange peel: curved solidified strip with Voronoi pores and a white pith edge.
- Licorice root: twisted fibrous cylinders. Ginger: slices with a fibrous cross-section.
- Poppy seeds: about 3,000 instanced kidney meshes.
- Heaps are settled with a 2-minute Bullet rigid-body drop, then applied.

PROPS
- Brass apothecary balance: lathe profiles, chains of arrayed tori. Brass is metallic (0.85, 0.62, 0.32), roughness 0.2-0.35 with smudge noise, and olive tarnish in cavities.
- Maceration jar: screw-modifier profile with a real 3 mm wall. A linen bag of botanicals hangs in it, draped once with a 20-frame cloth sim, then static.
- Background props, always soft: stone mortar, enamel desk lamp.

LIGHT
- Sun lamp at 0.53° through the real window frame, so the moving shadows are physically correct. Elevation is keyed 2°→6° and colour 3500K→5000K across Act I.
- 2x3 m sky area light outside the window at 7000K.
- Warm white bounce card and black flag planes.
- 2700K practical desk lamp for S05.
- Light groups: sun, sky, lamp.

CAMERA: 100 mm macro (S01, S02), 65 mm (S03), 85 mm (S04, S05). f/2-4. Motion-control slides of 2-12 cm.

RENDER: diffuse 3, glossy 3, transmission 10 (jar only), adaptive sampling at 96-128 spp, OIDN. Persistent data stays on across the five shots.

sets.name: B — The Cask Cellar (S06-S08; the end-slate background)
sets.build:
VAULT: a whitewashed brick barrel vault, 4 m wide, 12 m deep and 3 m high.
- Geometry Nodes instances bevelled bricks along the arc with 8 mm mortar gaps.
- Per-brick colour, roughness and scale jitter. Efflorescence and rising damp come from a height gradient multiplied by noise.
- Only the first three bays are lit; the rest falls to black.
- Floor: bevelled Voronoi flagstones with damp roughness variation.

CASKS: one Geometry Nodes generator for large oak casks, about 1.1 m tall.
- 24 staves, each with random width, hue and roughness, bulged along a profile.
- Coopering tool-mark bands. Iron hoops: scaled tori with a noise-masked rust layer and a little displacement.
- Heads chalked with numerals. No handwriting font is installed, so each digit (1, 9, 3, 4, 5) is a hand-authored stroke polyline with per-stroke jitter, pressure-varying width and grainy chalk alpha.
- 14 linked instances on bevelled timber cradles.

OCULUS: a Ø60 cm round window high in the end wall. Deep brick reveal, plain old glass in a single iron ring. No cross bars.

LIGHT
- Sun lamp at 0.53°, driven by a Python 'calendar' that keys azimuth, elevation and colour temperature for every rendered frame. One sweep per beat, so 6 'days' each stand for 2 months. Small random intensity jitter (±4%) mimics time-lapse exposure flicker.
- The light shaft is faked, never volumetric: a transparent card with 2% emission, a gradient and noise falloff, aligned to the sun and parented to it.
- An area light at the oculus, hidden from camera rays, fakes the bounce and kills small-window noise.
- Path guiding on (a Cycles CPU feature).
- Mist pass for depth haze, graded blue-grey.

CAMERA: 35 mm dolly-back of 2.5 m with a 40 cm boom; 100 mm macro on a cask head; 50 mm looking up at the oculus.

RENDER: about 96 spp, time-lapse portions rendered on twos.

REUSE: an S07 frame re-rendered at 512 spp, darkened and slightly blurred, becomes the end slate.

sets.name: C — Freighter Hold, North Atlantic 1970s (S09-S10)
sets.build:
HULL: a 6x4 m section of a 1970s freighter hold.
- Curved steel frames swept along curves every 60 cm, with plate seams. Geometry Nodes rivets along the edges.
- Layered paint: chipped green over red primer over rust and steel, driven by a noise chip mask with edge wear.
- A cargo net hangs from hooks.

PORTHOLE: riveted brass ring, Ø32 cm. The glass is reflection plus thin transmission (no refraction stack).
- Outside: a procedural Ocean-modifier plane (steel-grey swell) under a Nishita dusk sky and a cool sun. Always defocused.

CRATES: slatted pine crates.
- Bevelled planks with nail heads; rough-sawn pine from stretched noise with saw-mark bands.
- Stencils drawn with PIL in Liberation Sans Bold, with stencil bridges cut by script and overspray noise: 'MADE IN WEST GERMANY', 'ZERBRECHLICH · FRAGILE', 'CONSIGNEE: SIDNEY FRANK IMPORTING CO. · NEW YORK'.
- About 3,000 straw hair curves between the slats.
- Green bottle necks are instances of the hero bottle, at 4 transmission bounces (small and soft).

LAMP: a 1 cm point light at 2700K with an emissive filament inside a real wire cage (curves and tori), so it throws hard moving shadows. It swings on a damped-pendulum expression, phase-lagged against the ship's roll.

MOTION: the whole set is parented to an empty that rolls ±2° on a 7 s period.

CAMERA: 35 mm pull-back of 2 m at f/2.8; 85 mm insert on the stencil.

ATMOSPHERE: Mist pass haze only. Everything outside the lamp's pool falls to black, so the build stays small. About 64-96 spp.

sets.name: D — 1980s Back Bar, tap-machine corner (S11-S12)
sets.build:
A tabletop of about 1.2x0.6 m, built as a re-dress of Set E's back-bar corner (the same bar, a decade earlier), relit with fluorescent light.

MACHINE: an unbranded three-bottle ice-cold tap machine.
- Bevelled stainless body (40x30x55 cm): anisotropic metal with a noise-driven brushed tangent and fingerprint smudges in roughness.
- Black powder-coat collars hold three inverted hero bottles.
- Perforated drip grille made with a brick-texture alpha.
- Frost: a noise-thresholded white rough coat with micro-bump, plus about 20,000 Geometry Nodes-instanced ice-crystal flakes on the spout tip and collars only. Crystal scale is calibrated to 0.2-1 mm so it reads as frost, not snow.

BAR MAT: black rubber with a Geometry Nodes grid of studs.

SHOT GLASS: heavy base, 6 cm tall. A frosted-patch mask mixes clear and rough (0.35) transmission, with a few melt beads.

LIGHT
- A 120x4 cm area light overhead at 4000K, visible as a long soft highlight on the steel.
- A red neon smear: an out-of-focus emissive card.
- The back bar is a pre-rendered blurred plate on an emissive card, so only the spout, the stream, the glass and the mat are path-traced.
- A round enamel pendant with an emissive diffuser disc, placed so its reflection lands dead centre on the poured shot (S12).

CAMERA: 100 mm macro at f/4. Low angle for the pour; straight down for the reflection.

RENDER: transmission 12, caustics off, filter glossy 1.0, clamp indirect 4.

sets.name: E — Tahoe Lodge Bar, c.1997, summer blue hour (S13-S16, S21-S22; source of the glass-stage panorama)
sets.build:
ROOM: 7x5 m, knotty-pine walls.
- Wave-texture rings distorted around Voronoi knot cells, darker stain in the knots, a clear varnish coat. Baked to 4K.
- Dark plank floor.

BAR COUNTER: 3.5 m of lacquered fir.
- Coat 1.0, coat roughness 0.04, with a stretched-noise micro-scratch map and cup-ring ghosts.
- Brass foot rail. Cork coasters, a folded bar towel (one static cloth drape).

STOOLS: four chrome bar stools, lathe-modelled.
- Chrome is metallic at roughness 0.06-0.12 with scratch anisotropy.
- Red vinyl seats: wrinkle bump, a crack mask and sheen.

BACK BAR: shelves of about 30 unlabelled bottle silhouettes (simplified dark glass, 4 bounces), always out of focus.

WINDOW: 2.4x1.4 m, four panes, facing east over the lake (the bar is on the west shore, so the moon rises over the Carson Range).
- Thin-glass shader (Fresnel mix of transparent and glossy) with smudge roughness and a faint reflection of the pendants.
- Behind it, the E-X exterior plate sits on an emission card 30 m out. The moon is on its own layer so it can rise in 2D.

NEON: the word 'OPEN' in block letters, built from hand-authored centreline Bézier curves (no script font is installed) and mirrored, because we see it from inside.
- 12 mm glass tubes with an emission core in pink #FF4F9A, painted black-out sleeves at the joins, a backing frame, wires and a transformer box.
- A spill area light in its own light group, so flicker, ignition and death are animated in comp.

PENDANTS: three enamel shades over 2700K spot lights with emissive diffusers.

LIGHT GROUPS: MOON/SKY (window portal area light at 7500K plus the plate), NEON, PENDANTS, BACKBAR.

ATMOSPHERE: Mist pass haze, no volumes.

CAMERAS
- 85 mm through the window (S13).
- 50 mm slider 3 cm above the bar top (S14).
- 50 mm on the stool at f/1.8 (S15).
- 100 mm macro on the frost ring (S16).
- 85 mm packshot (S21).
- 35 mm on the neon (S22).

PANORAMA: once the set is dressed, render a 4096x2048 equirectangular panorama from the highball's position, with the glasses hidden, at 1024 spp adaptive. Save it as EXR. It becomes the world for Set F. This is our own render, not an external HDRI.

sets.name: E-X — Tahoe Exterior Plate (render-once still, only ever seen out of focus through the window)
sets.build:
TERRAIN: a 10x3 km ridge band placed 9-15 km away (compressed for the lens).
- A Geometry Nodes grid displaced by ridged multifractal plus noise.
- Summer: no snow at all. Pale granite greys, with a dark conifer band painted as texture (no individual trees).

LIGHT
- A warm low sun lamp at about 2800K, light-linked to the peaks only, gives the last alpenglow.
- Built-in Nishita sky with the sun at -3° for an indigo blue hour.
- The moon: an emission disc with noise 'maria' on a separate view layer, plus a weak cool sun for the long moon glade on the water.

LAKE: a glossy plane with a fine wave bump, mirror-calm.

RENDER: 4096x1716 EXR at 256 spp, with the moon as a separate layer.

REUSE: one render serves S13, S14, S15, S21 and S22 and is visible in the panorama. At f/2-2.8 on 85 mm it is always soft, so terrain detail never resolves. There is deliberately no wide exterior shot in the film.

sets.name: F — Glass Stage (liquid macro rig lit by the in-house bar panorama; S17-S20, packshot glass)
sets.build:
SCENE: only the glass, the liquid and an 80x50 cm patch of real bar top (the same lacquered fir) for correct contact shadows and reflections.
- World: the Set E equirectangular panorama.
- Real lights matching the panorama's practicals, for crisp speculars and shadows: a large cool area light behind at 7500K (the moon window), a warm 2700K pendant spot above and in front, and a pink neon kicker.
- Black flag planes left and right carve dark edge lines into the glass.
- Nothing near the glass comes from the panorama: the coaster, bar edge and towel are real geometry. That avoids fixed-point parallax errors.

HIGHBALL: straight-sided, 340 ml, 3 mm wall, 8 mm base.
- IOR 1.52, faint green absorption, smudge roughness 0-0.08.

SHOT GLASS: heavy base, 4 cl, 6 cm tall, frosted-patch mask.

LIQUIDS: overlap method, with each liquid mesh 0.2 mm inside the glass wall.
- Energy drink: IOR 1.34, pale gold-green Volume Absorption (0.95, 0.80, 0.30) at density 4, plus a Volume Scatter of 0.02 for a slight haze.
- Jägermeister: IOR 1.355, Volume Absorption (0.45, 0.10, 0.04) at density 120. Only absorption gives the true ruby edge around a near-black core.

CARBONATION: a Geometry Nodes Simulation Zone.
- Points spawn at nucleation sites on the floor and walls, rise with wobble and grow; a ring of bubbles clings at the meniscus.
- About 400 bubbles, shaded with a cheap thin glossy-plus-transparent mix instead of true refraction.

CONDENSATION: a Geometry Nodes scatter of flattened droplets from 0.2 to 3 mm, with a power-law size spread.
- Real geometry on the camera-facing side only (frustum mask), with a fogged-roughness mask between droplets.

SHADOW PROXY (S17): a shot glass with liquid that is invisible to camera rays but casts shadow. Its shader uses Light Path 'Is Shadow Ray' to switch to a ruby-tinted Transparent BSDF, so the shadow has a ruby core even with caustics off.

RENDER: transmission 12, glossy 4, diffuse 2, transparent 16, caustics off, filter glossy 1.0, clamp indirect 4, adaptive at 128-192 spp, OIDN. Always framed tight, and always shot from outside the glass.

sets.name: G — End Slate
sets.build:
A near-black oak-grain plate: an S07 cask-head frame re-rendered at 512 spp, darkened by about 85% and given a 4 px blur. Animated grain keeps it alive.

Type is rendered with PIL as alpha plates and composited. One Cycles render in total.

simulations:
SIM 1 — TAP POUR (Mantaflow FLIP liquid). Reused in S11 (side), S12 (top-down, settled final mesh), and as the frosted shot in S14.
- Domain 6x6x12 cm at true scale, resolution 160 (about 0.75 mm cells), time scale 0.5 for 2x slow motion.
- Inflow: a Ø5 mm cylinder at the spout, flowing for 0.6 s with a slight viscosity increase.
- Obstacle: the frosted shot glass with fractions on and a real 3 mm wall.
- Mesh upres 2, smoothing 2, speed vectors on. About 90 cache frames.
- Bake about 1-1.5 h after a resolution-80 test.

SIM 2 — HERO PLUNGE (Mantaflow FLIP liquid with spray, foam and bubbles). One bake, seen from three angles: S18 side profile, S19 top-down, S20 through the beaded wall. The settled final frame also serves the packshot.
- Domain 8x8x13 cm (highball interior plus 4 cm headroom for the crown), resolution 176 (about 0.74 mm cells), time scale 0.1.
- Shot glass: animated obstacle. Released about 6 cm above the surface, so it hits at about 1.1 m/s, with a 3° tilt. The fall is keyed from a quick Bullet pre-pass. Contact is on cache frame 15, which is film frame 1020.
- Highball inner wall: static obstacle, fractions on.
- CFL 2, up to 12 timesteps per frame, surface tension on.
- Secondary particles at capped counts, rendered as a Cycles point cloud.
- Mesh upres 2, smoothing 2, speed vectors on (motion blur and SIM 3 guiding).
- About 220 cache frames, exported to Alembic with velocities. CacheFile override-frame drivers retime it for the speed ramp in S20, so nothing is re-baked.
- Bake about 4-5 h overnight after a resolution-96 test (about 25 min).

SIM 3 — JÄGERMEISTER PLUME (Mantaflow gas, coupled to SIM 2). Used in S19-S20.
- Same bounds as SIM 2, resolution 96 with noise upres 2.
- Guides: velocity source set to Domain, guide parent = the baked SIM 2 domain, weight 0.85. The plume follows the real crown turbulence instead of drifting independently.
- Flow: the shot glass's interior volume as a smoke inflow, starting once it is submerged and lasting 0.25 s. It moves with the glass obstacle; the highball wall is an effector.
- Slightly negative buoyancy so it sinks and curls; vorticity 0.25; no dissipation.
- Rendered as an absorption-only volume in mahogany (0.35, 0.12, 0.04), density × 40, step rate 1-2, volume bounces 0. It is clipped below the animated liquid surface by an object-space Z mask keyed to the surface height.
- Bake about 30-40 min.
- Fallback: a Geometry Nodes Simulation Zone advects about 20k points by SIM 2's mesh velocities (Sample Nearest Surface) plus curl noise, then Points to Volume.

Not counted as simulations, all near-free:
- Bullet rigid-body settles of the botanical heaps (2 min) and the SIM 2 fall pre-pass.
- One 20-frame cloth drape for the linen bag.
- Geometry Nodes Simulation Zones for carbonation bubbles, condensation and the running melt bead.
- Python expressions for the balance, the swinging lamps, the stool spin and the typebars.

shots.description:
S01 TYPEBAR (frames 0-75). Black, then the opening orchestral hit at f0. Over 12 frames a low winter dawn finds the scene through the east window.

Extreme macro, 100 mm at f/2.8, locked off with a 2 cm motion-control drift right: the type basket of a 1930s office typewriter, a cream index card rolled on the black platen, a two-tone ribbon.

On the beats at f15, f30, f45 and f60, a typebar flicks up out of soft focus, slaps through the ribbon and retreats. The carriage escapes one 2.54 mm step each time, and four fresh glyphs complete the header '...WOLFENBÜTTEL 1934'. The new ink is a hair blacker and glossier than the rest. Diagonal mullion shadows lie across the card.

No keys or hands are in frame. VO 1 enters at 2.75, after the final '4'.
shots.cg_build:
Typewriter rig from Set A. Each strike is keyed by Python: rise in 3 frames ease-in, 1 frame of contact, return in 4 frames. The carriage translates on the contact frame; the ribbon vibrator lifts.

The four new glyphs are separate PIL alpha masks switched on at f15/30/45/60, each with a 1-frame wet-gloss boost. Their bump makes the impressions catch the light.

Motion blur at 180°. The sun lamp's elevation moves 2°→3.5° over the shot.

96 spp adaptive, diffuse 3 / glossy 3, OIDN. About 35 s/frame × 75 frames.

Botanical kit heaps, settled with Bullet then applied, on kraft paper over the baked oak bench.

Real displacement only inside the focus strip; bump everywhere else in the blur. Poppy seeds are about 3,000 instances. Subsurface and translucency on saffron, orange peel and cardamom.

128 spp adaptive. About 40 s/frame × 60 frames.

shots.description:
S03 BALANCE (frames 135-180). 65 mm at f/2.8, eye level: a brass apothecary balance.
- Left pan: heaped juniper and star anise. Right pan: small stamped brass weights.
- The beam sways in a damped oscillation. The pointer crosses centre twice and settles dead centre exactly on f180 (bar 4 downbeat), as we cut.
- The window blooms soft behind.

VO 2 'Fifty-six herbs...' begins at 6.25.
shots.cg_build:
Beam rotation: θ = 0.9°·e^(−t/0.55)·sin(2π·1.3t), solved by script so it settles on f180. The pans hang level via constraints.

Pan contents reuse the S02 instances. Brass shader from Set A, with smudges and cavity tarnish.

96 spp. About 25 s/frame × 45 frames.

Jar with a 3 mm wall. The liquid's Volume Absorption is keyed from clear, through (0.55, 0.25, 0.08), to (0.35, 0.10, 0.04), with density 0→60.

Sun rotation is stepped per rendered frame; sky strength dips for the nights.

Rendered on twos: 23 unique frames. Transmission 10, clamp 4. About 70 s per unique frame.

shots.description:
S05 GEHEIM (frames 225-300). 85 mm at f/2.8, a top-down drift over the typed recipe card in mixed window light and 2700K desk-lamp light.
- Header: 'KRÄUTERLIKÖR — REZEPTUR — C. MAST — WOLFENBÜTTEL 1934'.
- Below it, a numbered list in which every ingredient has been overtyped XXXXXXXX, the period typist's way of hiding words. The numbers stay soft and are never featured.
- The move eases and settles exactly centred on a round red rubber stamp: GEHEIM (secret). It is sized at 30% of picture height for the match cut at f300.

VO 3 'Which ones? Still a secret.' at 9.75.
shots.cg_build:
Same card shader as S01, with a second PIL page.
- Overtyping is double-struck Courier glyphs, with ink build-up and embossing via bump from the blurred glyph mask.
- Stamp ink breaks up with noise and pools at the edges.
- The desk-lamp filament dips once (keyed strength).

Diffuse only. About 15 s/frame × 75 frames.

shots.description:
S06 THE YEAR (frames 300-390). MATCH CUT on the bar 6 downbeat: the head of an oak cask, chalked '1934', fills the stamp's circle at the same size and position.

Motion-control dolly back 2.5 m with a 40 cm boom up, 35 mm at f/4. It reveals a whitewashed brick barrel vault: two rows of casks on timber cradles, worn flagstones.

High in the end wall, a round oculus throws a disc of sunlight. Time-lapse: the disc sweeps across the cask heads once per beat, six 'days' each standing for two months. Its colour runs from cold blue-white winter, to pale spring, hard white summer, amber autumn and blue again.

Everything outside the light falls to near black. VO 4 'Then it waits. A full year, in oak.' at 13.25.
shots.cg_build:
Set B. A Python calendar keys the sun lamp per rendered frame. The faked light-shaft card is parented to the sun; a hidden bounce light sits at the oculus. Path guiding on.

Rendered on twos: 45 unique frames. About 45 s per unique frame.

shots.description:
S07 1935 (frames 390-450). 100 mm macro on the next cask head as the year's light keeps sliding over it.
- A single spider thread between hoop and stave catches the sun.
- Rack focus (with lens breathing) to the chalk: '1934' struck through, and a fresh '1935' beside it, with chalk dust still on the chime ledge.

narration.line: Nineteen thirty-four. Curt Mast perfects a recipe.
Fifty-six herbs, blossoms, roots and fruits.
Then it waits. A full year, in oak.
In the seventies, it crosses an ocean.
And America serves it ice cold.
Around nineteen ninety-seven... somebody has an idea.
Nobody knows exactly who. Everybody knows the name.
A year in oak. A second in glass.

music:
CUE: 'PATIENCE', an original orchestral and hybrid score made from real recorded samples. VSCO-2 CE supplies strings (sustain, spiccato, pizzicato, tremolo), F horns, trumpets, tenor trombones, tuba, bassoon, timpani, bass drum, cymbals, harp, piano, organ and chimes. VCSL supplies Bass Drum 1/2, Frame Drum, Toms, Rope-Tension Snare, Gong 1/2, Clash Cymbals and Claves. Synthesized layers: sub hits, risers, reverse swells. No choir.

GRID: 96 BPM in 4/4.
- 1 beat = 0.625 s = 15 frames. 1 bar = 2.5 s = 60 frames.
- 24 bars = 60.0 s = 1,440 frames.
- Every cut sits on a beat; every structural hit is on a bar downbeat.

KEY: D minor, driven by i–VI–III–VII (Dm–B♭–F–C). It lifts to D MAJOR at the plume bloom (bar 19).

LEITMOTIF 'PATIENCE': D–A–B♭–A. When the drink is born, it becomes D–A–B♮–A: the B♭ lifts to B natural, and the score transforms like the liquid.

FUSE TICK: a dry, mono, high-passed VCSL claves/woodblock click. It doubles in speed each era:
- half notes in Act I, quarter notes in Act II, eighths in Act III, sixteenths at Tahoe;
- it stops dead at f1005;
- it returns once at f1425.

BAR MAP

BAR 1 | 0.000 | f0 | OVERTURE HIT
- Tuba, three trombones and a bassoon on D1/D2 sfz with a 4 s decay. Timpani D2, VCSL Bass Drum 1, a 41 Hz sub sine with a 3 s tail.
- A tubular chime on D, like a distant church bell, in the long hall.
- Typebar foley lands exactly on f15, f30 and f45. A cello and bass D pedal enters pp under the decay.

BAR 2 | 2.500 | f60
- The last typebar strike plus felt piano D3.
- The fuse tick starts in half notes (f60, f90...).
- Solo F horn states PATIENCE mp in half notes: D4 f60, A4 f90, B♭4 f120, A4 f150. Ducked under VO 1.

BAR 3 | 5.000 | f120
- Harp harmonics answer. Violas and cellos start a spiccato 8th-note ostinato (D D A D F D A D), pp rising to mp. Pizzicato basses on beats 1 and 3.
- f135 (cut, balance): a pizzicato and harp pluck. Chords Dm → B♭.

BAR 4 | 7.500 | f180
- The balance settles on a soft timpani tap.
- Jar time-lapse: the ostinato doubles to 16ths and a harp glissando rises. Each 'day' flicker gets a brushed suspended-cymbal swell. Gm (f180) → A (f210).
- f225 (cut, card): a low piano octave D.

BAR 5 | 10.000 | f240 | GEHEIM
- Trombones pp: Gm → A(sus4→3).
- Timpani roll crescendo from f270, with a reverse cymbal into f300.

BAR 6 | 12.500 | f300 | HIT 1 (mf→f) on the stamp-to-cask match cut
- Timpani D, bass drum, low brass D, soft crash.
- The fuse moves to quarter notes. Four horns and cellos in octaves play PATIENCE in half notes over string tremolo.
- Seasons harmony changes every half bar: Dm (f300), B♭ (f330). Each sun sweep (every beat) gets a pizzicato accent.

BAR 7 | 15.000 | f360
- F (f360), C (f390). Violins join with spiccato 16ths. Snare roll pp from f390 (cut S07). The horns swell.

BAR 8 | 17.500 | f420 | '1935'
- Timpani plus a suspended-cymbal choke, synced to the chalk and the year counter.
- Synth riser (filtered noise plus a rising saw), a suspended-cymbal roll and string crescendo.
- f450 (cut, oculus): horns crescendo. A reversed crash and reverse-reverb swell lead into f480.

BAR 9 | 20.000 | f480 | HIT 2 (ff) on the oculus-to-porthole match cut
- Sub boom with a 45→30 Hz pitch drop, two layered bass drums, VCSL frame drum and low toms played taiko-style, timpani D, crash.
- Low brass holds a D–A 'ship-horn' fifth for two beats.
- Then the MARCH: a rope-tension snare ostinato; tuba, bassoon and basses on a D–D–F–E quarter-note ostinato; the fuse in 8ths.

BAR 10 | 22.500 | f540
- Four horns play PATIENCE f across bars 10-11 in half notes. Chords B♭ → F.
- f555 (cut, stencil): snare fill. f585 (cut, pour): cymbal choke plus a timpani hit.

BAR 11 | 25.000 | f600 | AMERICA
- Two trumpets take PATIENCE up a fifth (A–E–F–E), bright and open, over full spiccato strings, with timpani on beats 1 and 3. Chords C → A.
- f630 (cut, disc): the trumpets hold.
- A reverse swell rises toward f660 and is cut dead.

BAR 12 | 27.500 | f660 | DEAD CUT
- Orchestra and fuse stop on the exact frame of the moon match cut.
- Left: room tone, lake lap, faint synthesized crickets, a high violin harmonic A5 ppp, a harp harmonic D.
- f690: the neon ignites, and its 120 Hz buzz becomes the pedal tone.

BAR 13 | 30.000 | f720
- Piano callback A4 (f720) and F4 (f750), echoing the opening. Cello tremolo D pp.
- The fuse returns in 16ths at about -30 dB, quiet and insistent, rising about 2 dB per bar.

BAR 14 | 32.500 | f780
- Sub heartbeat: soft-mallet bass drum plus a 40 Hz sine on beats 1 and 3, doubled by pizzicato basses.
- f795 (cut, stool): felt piano D2.

BAR 15 | 35.000 | f840
- Violin tremolo begins to climb a step per bar (E, F, G, then the impact). Heartbeat continues.
- f870 (cut, frost ring).

BAR 16 | 37.500 | f900
- Strings on F. The heartbeats at f900, f930, f960 and f990 drive the meniscus tremble in S17.
- Timpani roll from f930. Riser 2 runs 4.4 s to f1005.

BAR 17 | 40.000 | f960
- Strings on G. Low brass plays PATIENCE in quarter notes under the riser (D f960, A f975, B♭ f990, held). Snare roll from f975. A reversed crash ends exactly at f1005.
- f1005-1019: ONE BEAT OF TOTAL SILENCE. Music, fuse, room tone, neon and fizz all go to digital zero with 2-frame fades.

BAR 18 | 42.500 | f1020 | IMPACT (fff)
- Sub-impact with a 45→28 Hz drop, two concert bass drums plus a VCSL bass drum, timpani D and A.
- Low brass and horns stab a B♭/D chord: the dark VI over the tonic pedal, unresolved. Clash cymbals and a VCSL gong swell.
- The synthesized glass-plunge layer (see sound design).
- The brass B♭ chord then swells under string tremolo with a timpani roll crescendo.
- f1050 (cut, top-down): a rising cymbal swell, and a reverse gong into f1080.

BAR 19 | 45.000 | f1080 | THE BLOOM, MAJOR
- The harmony turns to D major (F♯ in the violins).
- Four horns and two trumpets in unison, ff, sing the transformed motif: D (f1080), A (f1095), B♮ (f1110, held two beats: the B♭ has become B natural), A (f1140).
- Soaring string 16ths, an upward harp glissando, an organ pedal D at 16' and 32', bass drum and low tom on beats 1 and 3.
- From f1110 a fizz rush rides the speed ramp.

BAR 20 | 47.500 | f1140 | TITLE HIT
- Timpani, bass drum and crash; the brass holds D major, then pulls back to strings and horns under the title card. No voice.

BAR 21 | 50.000 | f1200 | HERO HIT
- Full tutti in D major with organ, bass drums and crash.
- Trumpets and horns state the motif one last time in augmentation (D f1200, A f1230, B f1260, A f1290), ducked about 5 dB under VO 9.

BAR 22 | 52.500 | f1260
- A plagal turn: G/D (f1260) → D (f1290). Strings soar, harp shimmer, the decrescendo begins.

BAR 23 | 55.000 | f1320
- The score thins to strings and an organ D. The neon stutters (55.2, 55.4) and dies with a click on f1335.
- One beat of near silence. f1350 (cut, slate): a low chime D and string harmonics.

BAR 24 | 57.500 | f1380 | BUTTON
- A short tutti on the wordmark: timpani D, bass drum, a low-brass D major chord, organ D.
- It rings out with string harmonics and the opening tubular chime as a bookend.
- A single fuse tick at f1425 (59.375). Silence at f1440.

PRODUCTION
- Write the MIDI with mido (PPQ 480). Every hit time is computed from its frame number divided by 24, so the audio is frame-locked to the cut.
- Render with a small NumPy sampler over the VSCO-2 CE and VCSL WAVs:
  - velocity layers and round-robins, with no sample repeated back-to-back;
  - natural release tails;
  - legato horn lines from overlapped sustains with 60-80 ms crossfades;
  - timing humanised by ±8 ms, except the frame-locked hits.
- Epic weight without a choir:
  - double the four horns into eight virtual horns (two passes, 10 ms offset, ±4 cents detune);
  - trombones a3 plus tuba plus bassoon in the low register;
  - two layered string passes, panned wide;
  - organ 16' and 32' at the climax;
  - a bass drum, frame drum and tom ensemble in place of taiko;
  - a VCSL gong for the swells;
  - sub sines from 28 to 45 Hz.
- One shared convolution hall: a synthesized IR with a 2.6 s RT60 and 25 ms pre-delay. A short room for the foley.
- Light 2:1 bus compression and a limiter.

MIX
- The VO sidechains the music down 4-6 dB.
- Loudness peaks are reserved for f0, f480, f1020, f1080, f1200 and f1380.
- Masters: -14 LUFS integrated for web, -23 LUFS for broadcast, -1 dBTP true peak.
sound_design:
PHILOSOPHY: restrained, close and real-sounding foley built from synthesis and percussion samples. No external recordings. The soundtrack has three silences: the dead cut at f660, total digital silence at f1005-1019, and the near-silence after the neon dies.

ACT I, WORKROOM
- Room tone: low-passed pink noise with a soft wind gust at the window.
- Typebar strikes (f15, f30, f45, f60), layered:
  - a 180 Hz key 'thunk' sine of 20 ms;
  - a typebar slap (noise burst high-passed at 2 kHz, 8 ms);
  - a platen 'thock' (band-pass at 400 Hz);
  - an escapement tick (VCSL claves, pitched up);
  - no carriage bell.
- S02: a dry botanical rustle (granular, high-passed crackle) riding the slider.
- S03: chain tinkle from small inharmonic modal tones, and a pivot tick as the pointer settles.
- S04: a soft filtered-noise 'day' swell per light flicker, and a faint glass ring.
- S05: card flex.

ACT II, CELLAR
- A large stone room tone with deep air.
- Each sun sweep gets a low filtered-noise 'whoomp' (the days passing).
- At f420, a quick chalk scratch, granular and high-passed.
- No dripping sounds anywhere.

ACT III
- Hold: hull groan (a slow resonant low-pass sweep on a pitched-down saw), steel and timber creaks (VCSL friction idiophones, pitched), sea wash through the porthole (LFO-filtered noise), a lamp-chain squeak in time with the swing.
- Tap machine: compressor hum (60 Hz plus harmonics), a liquid stream (modulated band-pass noise plus bubble chirps), and a rising-pitch resonance as the shot glass fills.
- S12: fluorescent tube hum.

ACT IV, TAHOE
- After the dead cut: lake lap, faint crickets (4.5 kHz sine pulse trains, very low), room tone.
- Neon ignition at f690: transformer buzz (120 Hz plus harmonics, US mains), crackle and tick-tick on the stutters.
- Bar: refrigerator hum, close fizz (dense high exponential-chirp bubble pops), a slow squeaking swivel bearing on the stool.
- The heartbeat lives in the score.
- f1005-1019: everything at digital zero.

ACT V, THE SECOND
- f1020 glass plunge, layered:
  - a deep muffled boom (50 Hz sine plus noise low-passed at 300 Hz);
  - a splash: a granular noise burst time-stretched 4x and pitched down for the slow motion;
  - crown tearing (a high noise shimmer);
  - reversed bubble chirps for the hanging droplets;
  - a reverse-gong tail.
- About 44.4 s: a muted glass 'tonk' (modal synthesis) as the shot glass touches bottom.
- f1080: a low swirling 'ink' tone under the bloom.
- f1110-1130: a fizz rush pitched from slowed to normal speed as the speed ramp returns to real time.
- Packshot: real-time fizz, bar room tone, neon hum, a tiny condensation slide on the bead.
- 55.2/55.4: neon stutters, then the death click on f1335, then the transformer ring-down. The room falls to lake lap only.
- f1425: a single fuse tick.

VOICE (the client's main complaint)
Engine choice:
- Kokoro (kokoro-onnx), which very likely produced the rejected voice, is excluded except as an A/B control.
- Primary candidates: Supertonic-3 male styles M1-M5 through sherpa-onnx (a flow-matching model with more natural prosody). Use speed 0.85-0.95 and more synthesis steps.
- Secondary: the Piper VITS male voices (en_US ryan-high, norman, joe, hfc_male; en_GB alan, northern_english_male) with length_scale 1.1-1.2, noise_scale 0.6-0.75 and noise_w 0.8.
- ZipVoice may only be prompted with our own best synthetic take, never with a real person's recording.
- Pocket-TTS is skipped: its licence is non-commercial and its prompts are real voices.

Shoot-out:
- Render each of the 10 lines in 5 takes for every candidate voice.
- Screen automatically with the installed DNSMOS (keep overall score 3.3 or higher) and Whisper-small.en (zero transcription errors apart from the brand name). Prefer a naturally low median F0, around 110 Hz or below.
- Then pick by ear among the top three takes per line.

Text preparation:
- Write numbers as words.
- If needed, respell names phonetically: 'Yay-ger-my-ster', 'Kurt Mahst'.
- Generate each line separately. The two-sentence lines (4, 8, 9) are generated as two clips and the pause is edited, never time-stretched.

Direction: a deep bass-baritone around 55, close-mic, unhurried, warm chest, a touch of gravel, understated authority. Never the shouty trailer cliché.

Post chain (ffmpeg):
- highpass 60 Hz;
- low shelf +2.5 dB at 120 Hz; -2.5 dB at 300 Hz; +1.5 dB at 3 kHz;
- deesser;
- acompressor 3:1, attack 15 ms, release 120 ms;
- a touch of asoftclip for chest;
- a 0.35 s synthesized small-room IR through afir at -20 dB, so the voice is not dead-dry;

render_plan:
FORMAT
- Render 1920x804 (2.39:1) and composite into a 1920x1080 master with 138 px bars.
- 24 fps, 1,440 timeline frames.
- Deliver ProRes 422 HQ plus H.264 for web. Audio: 48 kHz WAV mixed with picture, plus AAC 320k.

GLOBAL CYCLES SETTINGS (Blender 5.2, CPU, 4 cores)
- AgX view transform.
- Adaptive sampling: noise threshold 0.02 (0.015 on heroes), minimum 16 spp.
- OIDN with albedo and normal passes, prefilter Accurate.
- Light tree on. Persistent data on.
- Path guiding on for Sets B, C and E.
- Caustics off. Filter glossy 1.0. Clamp indirect 4.
- Bounces:
  - non-glass sets: diffuse 3, glossy 3, transmission 6;
  - glass shots: transmission 12, glossy 4, diffuse 2, transparent 16.
- Volumes: step rate 1-2, bounces 0.
- Motion blur only on moving shots: 180°, or 45° for slow motion. Animated seed.
- Passes: Mist, depth, light groups, Cryptomatte.

COMPOSITING
- Lens finish, grain and halation as in the visual language.
- tmedian over 3 frames on locked-off shots, to steady any OIDN shimmer.
- Supers and subtitles as PIL plates.
